SQX144-EV-000002.title: UI supervises the engine over a reconnecting WebSocket and dies with it
SQX144-EV-000002.question: How does the desktop UI detect engine death and coordinate shutdown?

claim.statement: The Electron main process holds a ReconnectingWebSocket to ws://127.0.0.1:<port>/websocket/app (connectionTimeout 5000 ms, maxRetries 10). When retries are exhausted it probes GET /status and GET /exit, shows an engine-crashed dialog, and quits. Closing the window is prevented and {'action':'exitApp'} is sent to the backend; the app quits only when the backend commands exit.
limitations: Behavior read from the satellite side only; the Java side of /websocket/app was not decompiled.

SQX144-EV-000006.title: Form-urlencoded POSTs gzipped locally; token auth; cloud URL rewriting
SQX144-EV-000006.question: How are request payloads encoded and authenticated, and how does cloud mode differ?

claim.statement: Local-mode POSTs send form-urlencoded bodies gzipped with pako (Content-Encoding: gzip); cloud-mode POSTs are plain form-urlencoded and GETs use query params. Auth uses an sq-auth-token header obtained from POST /main/login and persisted in localStorage, or a Cognito Bearer token in cloud mode; window.top.requestsPrefix rewrites URLs for cloud/node routing.
limitations: Cloud behaviors read from client code paths; no cloud instance was exercised.

SQX144-EV-000009.title: Live updates flow over a project/channel pub-sub WebSocket
SQX144-EV-000009.question: How do live updates reach the web apps?

claim.statement: The client asks /main/getWebSocketPort, then connects ws://<host>:<port>/websocket/updates, sends {action:'setup', app:product}, and subscribes by projectName/channel with {action:'subscribe'|'unsubscribe'}; inbound messages {projectData:{name, channels:[{name,data}]}} are routed to per-channel callbacks registered with unique callback IDs (duplicate IDs rejected); general listeners receive all messages; disconnects trigger a 1-second reconnect loop; subscriptions to project 'TaskManager' are ignored client-side.
limitations: Server side (SQWebSocketServlet) not decompiled.
